questions.prompt: Which statement gives the core rule for “Strings, UTF-8, and slices”?
options: Cargo is the main tool for creating, building, and testing projects.
`String` owns the text; `&str` borrows a view.
Rust bindings are immutable unless declared mut.
Obtain the installer from rust-lang.org and install native prerequisites only for the target you need.
questions.answer: `String` owns the text; `&str` borrows a view.
questions.explanation:
`String` owns the text; `&str` borrows a view.
Why: A Rust `String` owns growable UTF-8 text on the heap; `&str` is a borrowed view. UTF-8 characters can use multiple bytes, so `text[0]` indexing is unavailable: `len()` counts bytes, while `chars()` iterates Unicode scalar values. A slice views part of text or an array without copying it; a function accepting `&str` can work with both a `String` and a string literal.
